chapter: Buck and Bubbles: Nazarro and Bubbles
title: Learning each step more than one way
summary: Chuckles never changed his style but Green kept inventing different ways to do each Bubbles step, and explained them to Bubbles to keep time.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: So tell me a little bit more about how you began to change your form of tap dancing and when that started to occur, and how Chuckles was reacting to that. Did he feel alienated, or feel a little bit left out, or was he feeling -- was he growing with you? Was he changing too?

No, no, no, no. He never changed. But he's the cause of it you see. They thought that -- see, I liked Mr. Bubbles' tap dancing so much that I learned one of his steps, I would go out somewhere on my own and see how many different ways I could do this particular step, you see. And eventually, I used to tell Mr. Bubbles what I was doing. And he said, 'Well, what's that? How could you do that?' And he would make me explain how I could do it. Well, he did just to make sure that I would be in time, I wouldnt get out of time, see. Like you're doing a rhythm, if you mess it up, you know, it's just like you go to write with a pencil. If you go to write a G and start to make it a J, it's not the
same thing, you see. So he was pleased.
